external_entities.name: user's browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser outside our network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: The web application that receives browser traffic and places jobs onto the message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: The web application does not do the heavy work itself. It puts jobs onto a message queue

processes.name: background worker process
processes.description: A background worker that picks up jobs and performs the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: The database read and written by the background worker and used to keep the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The description does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the web application reads its settings, including its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store from which the worker reads its settings, including its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

data_flows.name: browser requests to web application
data_flows.description: The user's browser talks to the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: web application enqueues jobs
data_flows.description: The web application puts jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: background worker picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: background worker accesses database
data_flows.description: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The description does not say how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: web application reads config
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from the web application config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config
data_flows.data_description: web application settings and queue credentials

data_flows.name: worker reads config
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from the worker config.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet, outside our network, where the user's browser sits.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier.

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier behind the web tier, containing the queue, worker and database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application is internet-facing because the user's browser reaches it across the public internet.
assumptions.basis: The description states that a user's browser talks to the web application across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker process is non-web because it is described as a background worker that picks up jobs and performs work rather than presenting a web interface.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies it as a background worker process that picks up jobs from a queue and does the work.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config is confidential because it holds the web application's queue credentials.
assumptions.basis: The description states that the web application config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config is confidential because it holds the worker's database credentials.
assumptions.basis: The description states that the worker config holds the credentials the process needs, specifically the worker's database credentials.
